states.name: Alaska
states.dui: Active THC — no legal limit, officer discretion
states.consume: Private property only. No public use.

notes.s: One of the first states to legalize (2014).
Old convictions eligible for expungement.
No licensed consumption lounges statewide.
Delivery limited by geography — rural areas vary.

states.name: Arizona
states.dui: Zero tolerance — any detectable THC

notes.s: Zero-tolerance DUI — even trace metabolites can count.
Home grow must be in an enclosed, secure space.
Approved by voters in 2020 (Prop 207).
Delivery is legal statewide.

states.name: California
states.tax: 15% excise + local taxes (can hit 35%+ in some cities)
states.dui: No legal limit — officer discretion + blood test
states.consume: Private residence. Licensed lounges in select cities.

notes.s: Some cities (e.g. Fresno) ban retail outright — check local laws.
Smoking where tobacco is banned = also banned.
Cannabis cafés and lounges licensed in L.A., San Francisco.
First medical state (1996). Combined taxes often 30–35%.
Delivery legal statewide — strong legal market.

states.name: Colorado
states.tax: 15% excise + 15% special sales tax + state/local sales
states.dui: 5 ng/mL blood THC (presumptive — rebuttable)
states.consume: Private property. Licensed lounges in Denver & Aspen.

notes.s: Denver has licensed cannabis-friendly hotels.
Pioneered recreational legalization in 2012.
Edibles are heavily regulated in labeling and dosing.
Strong retail market — prices are competitive.

states.name: Connecticut
states.possess: 1.5 oz on person · 5 oz at home
states.home: 3 mature + 3 immature per adult · INDOOR ONLY · outdoor = felony
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion + blood test
states.medAdv: 5 oz/month purchase, lower taxes, higher-potency products
states.consume: Private property only. No multi-unit building common areas.

notes.s: Outdoor growing is a felony — indoor only, even one plant outside.
Plants must not be visible from the street or neighboring properties.
Home grow legal for all adults since July 2023.
44,000+ cannabis convictions automatically expunged (Dec 2022).
Purchase limit is lower (0.5 oz/transaction) than most rec states.
Delivery is legal — 3 delivery-only operators in CT.

states.name: Delaware
states.purchase: 1 oz flower · 12g concentrate · 750mg THC per transaction
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: No home growing whatsoever — recreational or medical.
Retail launched August 1, 2025 — 12 converted medical dispensaries opened day one; 30 rec-only licenses still rolling out.
Small state — dispensary access is generally close.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.purchase: Cannot be sold — gifting market only
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Congress blocks DC from running retail sales — only 'gifting' exists.
Gifting: buy a sticker/shirt, receive weed as a 'free gift.'
Home grow is generous — 6 plants for personal use.
Medical dispensaries do sell directly — recreational loop is the gifting market.

states.name: Illinois
states.home: Home grow NOT permitted for recreational (medical patients: 5 plants)
states.purchase: Same as possession limits per visit
states.dui: 5 ng/mL whole blood per se limit (10 ng other bodily fluid) — medical cardholders exempt from per se
states.medAdv: Home grow rights, higher limits, tax discounts

notes.s: Out-of-state visitors get lower limits (15g vs 30g).
No recreational home grow — medical card required.
Strong social equity focus in licensing — minority-owned dispensaries.
Potency-based tax: flower taxed less than concentrates.

states.name: Maine
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.consume: Private property. Some licensed social clubs.

notes.s: Has licensed cannabis clubs — one of few states to allow them.
Very generous home grow (12 immature plants per adult).
Low 10% tax rate — among the lowest in legal states.
Delivery legal — smaller market, rural areas vary.

states.name: Maryland
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Recreational sales began July 2023 — still a maturing market.
Home grow: only 2 plants per adult, locked away from minors.
Medical program continues alongside recreational sales.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.possess: 1 oz on person · 10 oz at home
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion + blood
states.medAdv: More product variety, potential tax reduction
states.consume: Private property. Licensed social consumption in some towns.

notes.s: 10 oz home storage limit — one of the highest in the country.
Landlords can legally prohibit use in rental units.
Social consumption sites licensed — check your city.
Delivery legal — competitive market.

states.name: Michigan
states.possess: 2.5 oz on person · 10 oz at home
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: 12 plants per adult — most generous home grow in the US.
Very competitive retail market — some of the lowest prices nationally.
Plants must not be visible from public spaces or roads.
Delivery legal — widespread availability.

states.name: Minnesota
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Retail launched 2025 — dispensary availability still expanding.
800mg edible limit is among the higher in the country.
Check dispensary availability — rollout is ongoing.

states.name: Missouri
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: 3 oz possession limit — among the more generous rec states.
Prop 3 (2022) converted existing medical dispensaries to dual-use.
Low excise tax rate (6%) — prices tend to be competitive.

states.name: Montana
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Rural state — dispensaries concentrated in Billings, Missoula, Bozeman.
Retail began January 2022.
20% tax is on the higher end — prices reflect it.

states.name: Nevada
states.home: 6 plants per adult · max 12/household (only if 25+ miles from nearest dispensary)
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion (2 ng/mL retained for felony DUI only)
states.consume: Private property. Licensed lounges in Las Vegas area.

notes.s: Home grow ONLY if you live 25+ miles from a dispensary.
Hotels universally prohibit use. Casino floors are off-limits.
Possession limits raised to 2.5 oz flower / 7g concentrate on Jan 1, 2024 (SB 277).
Per se DUI limits repealed July 2025 (AB 400) — now impairment-based like most rec states.
Consumption lounges are licensed in Las Vegas area.

states.name: New Jersey
states.tax: 6.625% sales tax + local transfer tax (up to 3%)
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.consume: Private property. Licensed social lounges permitted.

notes.s: 6 oz possession limit — one of the highest in the US.
No home growing whatsoever — recreational or medical.
Low sales tax (6.6%) but local taxes can add up.
Delivery legal statewide.

states.name: New Mexico
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.consume: Private property. Licensed on-site consumption permitted.

notes.s: On-site consumption lounges are fully licensed — one of few states.
16g concentrate limit is among the most generous.
Retail launched June 2021.
Delivery legal statewide.

states.name: New York
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.consume: Anywhere tobacco smoking is legally permitted.

notes.s: Only state allowing use wherever tobacco is legal — parks, streets.
No use in cars, near schools, or on federal property.
24g concentrate limit is the highest among rec states.
Retail rollout was slow — market expanding rapidly now.

states.name: Ohio
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Legalized via Issue 2 in November 2023; sales launched August 6, 2024.
Cleared $700M+ in first-year recreational sales — established market with 150+ dual-use dispensaries.
120+ Ohio municipalities have moratoriums banning adult-use sales — check your city.

states.name: Oregon
states.possess: 1 oz in public · 8 oz at home · 16 oz solid edibles · 72 oz liquid
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.consume: Private property. Licensed consumption cafés exist.

notes.s: One of the most established markets — prices are very competitive.
Cannabis cafés licensed in Portland area.
Very generous home storage (8 oz flower, 72 oz liquid).
Delivery legal — strong infrastructure.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.possess: 1 oz on person · 10 oz at home
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: Retail launched December 2022.
10 oz home storage — generous for a small state.
Smallest state — dispensary access is rarely far.

states.name: Vermont
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion

notes.s: First state to legalize by legislature (not ballot), 2018.
Retail sales launched October 2022.
Boutique, slower-growing market with fewer dispensaries.

states.name: Virginia
states.possess: 1 oz in public (over 1 oz = civil fine, over 4 oz = criminal)
states.purchase: No recreational retail yet — sales begin July 1, 2027
states.tax: Retail tax structure pending — set by HB 30 (2026) for July 2027 launch
states.dui: No per se limit — officer discretion
states.medAdv: Medical dispensaries operate now — the ONLY legal way to purchase in Virginia today

notes.s: No legal recreational retail yet — possession is legal, buying it is not.
Gray/black market purchases carry legal risk despite possession being legal.
Possession & home grow legal since July 2021 (HB 2312).
HB 30 enacted June 29, 2026 — retail sales begin July 1, 2027; CCA must adopt regulations by Feb 1, 2027.
Home grow: 4 plants per household, out of public view.
Existing medical dispensaries expected to convert to dual-use in 2027.

states.name: Washington
states.possess: 1 oz flower · 7g concentrate · 16 oz solid edibles · 72 oz liquid

states.dui: 5 ng/mL blood THC limit
states.medAdv: Home grow rights (medical only), lower taxes

notes.s: 37% excise tax — highest in any legal state. Prices are steep.
No recreational home growing — medical card required for any plants.
5 ng/mL blood limit for DUI — strictly enforced.
